_about: TEMPLATE for the human-labeled golden-pair accuracy eval. Copy this file to 'golden_pairs.json' (same dir), replace the example pairs with your own labeled pairs, then run: python -m src.main eval-golden-pairs --pairs data/eval/golden_pairs/golden_pairs.json . The evaluator reads ONLY cached artifacts under outputs/eval/<persona>/ (no LLM, no fetching), so each pair's persona must have been run by `eval-resumes` first and both job ids must exist in that persona's final_ranking artifacts.

_schema.pair_id: string, unique within the file (e.g. gp-001)
_schema.persona: string, must match a folder under outputs/eval/ (e.g. backend_platform)
_schema.resume_path: string, informational only (the resume the persona used)
_schema.expected_winner: one of: A_better | B_better | tie | unsure  (this is the HUMAN label)
_schema.label_reason: string, why you labeled it this way (extractive/job-relative reasoning)
_schema.category: one of: same_domain_close | adjacent_vs_primary | seniority_gap | domain_transfer | tool_stack_gap | product_duty_vs_prerequisite | weak_vs_adjacent | mismatch_guard

_label_meaning.A_better: job A is the better-fit role for this resume; the system should rank A above B
_label_meaning.B_better: job B is the better-fit role; the system should rank B above A
_label_meaning.tie: genuinely too close to call; the system is 'correct' if it treats them as a near-tie (same fit_level)
_label_meaning.unsure: you cannot decide; EXCLUDED from accuracy scoring (reported only)

_a_b_convention: Order is arbitrary, but `propose-golden-pairs` emits A = the job the default mode (domain_fit_bt) ranks higher, so A_better = you agree with the system and B_better = you would flip it. You may order A/B however you like in hand-written pairs.
_note: fit_level is 1-5 and is NOT a pass probability. The accuracy %% reported by the evaluator is an eval-internal agreement metric (system vs your labels), not a product number.

pairs.label_reason: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE. A is a core backend/server role (primary domain) with Kotlin/Spring + RDB design directly matched; B is an adjacent devops/AIOps platform role with multiple missing core prerequisites (time-series DB, search engine, open-source platform ownership). A is the clearer fit for a backend platform resume.

ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE. Both are strong-domain backend roles, so this is a close same-domain call. A has no core prerequisite gap; B leaves 'robust service architecture design' as an unmet core prerequisite, so A is the slightly stronger fit.
ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE. Cross-discipline transfer: A is the candidate's primary backend domain; B is an ML/AI role (weak domain) with essentially all AI prerequisites missing. A is far better fit.
